factories.name: newListEventsStep
factories.description: List one page of a calendar view, the events and expanded recurring occurrences that overlap a bounded window, with every time returned at an explicit offset.

inputSchema.description: ListEventsInput selects one page of a calendar view: the occurrences, exceptions, and single instances of events that overlap a bounded window, with recurring series expanded.

calendarId.description: CalendarID is a calendar ID from the calendar picker; blank lists the mailbox's default calendar.

pageSize.description: PageSize is the maximum events in the page, from 1 to 250; zero requests 50. Graph may return fewer events, even none, before the last page.

pageToken.description: PageToken is the NextPageToken of the previous page. Keep every other field unchanged when paging.

timeMax.description: TimeMax is the required window end as RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. The window is at most 366 days.

timeMin.description: TimeMin is the required window start as RFC 3339 with an explicit offset.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is an optional IANA zone for the offsets of returned times; blank uses UTC.

factories.name: newGetEventStep
factories.description: Read one event by its Graph event ID.

inputSchema.description: GetEventInput identifies one event to read. Graph event IDs are unique within a mailbox, so no calendar ID is needed.

eventId.description: EventID is the Graph event ID, including an expanded occurrence ID.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is an optional IANA zone for the offsets of returned times; blank uses UTC.

factories.name: newCreateEventStep
factories.description: Create one timed or all-day event under the Step's idempotency key, sent as Graph's transactionId and stamped as an extended property for retry lookup.

EventAttendeeInput.description: EventAttendeeInput is one attendee supplied to createEvent or updateEvent.

email.description: Email is one bare SMTP address such as person@example.com, without a display name.

isOptional.description: IsOptional makes the attendee optional instead of required.

EventDateTime.description: EventDateTime is one event boundary: an absolute instant plus the IANA time zone it is shown in. DateTime is RFC 3339 with an explicit Z or ±hh:mm offset, such as 2026-02-24T09:00:00-08:00, and TimeZone is an IANA name such as America/Los_Angeles. The offset fixes the instant; TimeZone is the zone the event is written in, so Outlook keeps the organizer's zone. A value without an offset, such as 2026-02-24T09:00:00, or without TimeZone, is rejected rather than guessed. Microsoft Graph itself stores a wall time without an offset plus a zone name. The connector writes the wall time of the instant in TimeZone, or the UTC wall time when a daylight-saving change makes that wall time ambiguous, so the instant never moves. It reads every time back in UTC and returns it with an offset in the requested zone.

dateTime.description: DateTime is the RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is the IANA time zone of the boundary, such as America/Los_Angeles.

inputSchema.description: CreateEventInput describes one event to create. Every attempt of one Step execution uses the same idempotency key: TransactionID when set, otherwise the Step's Call ID. The key is sent as Graph's transactionId and stamped on the event as a connector-owned extended property, so a retried Step finds and returns its own event.

attendees.description: Attendees lists unique bare attendee addresses. Graph sends every attendee an invitation when the event is created, and that cannot be turned off; empty creates an event without attendees.

body.description: Body is the optional plain-text event body.

calendarId.description: CalendarID is a writable calendar ID from the calendar picker; blank uses the mailbox's default calendar.

end.description: End is the exclusive end; see EventDateTime and ValidateEventTimes.

isAllDay.description: IsAllDay creates an all-day event; Start and End must then be midnights in one zone.

location.description: Location is the optional location display name.

requestOnlineMeeting.description: RequestOnlineMeeting asks Graph to attach a Microsoft Teams meeting to the event.

start.description: Start is the inclusive start; see EventDateTime and ValidateEventTimes.

subject.description: Subject is the required event title.

transactionId.description: TransactionID optionally fixes the idempotency key for business-level deduplication across Step executions: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, hyphens, or underscores. Blank uses the Call ID.

factories.name: newUpdateEventStep
factories.description: Patch the subject, body, location, start and end, or attendees of one existing event after reading it, skipping a change it already holds and sending If-Match with its ETag.

EventAttendeeInput.description: EventAttendeeInput is one attendee supplied to createEvent or updateEvent.

email.description: Email is one bare SMTP address such as person@example.com, without a display name.

isOptional.description: IsOptional makes the attendee optional instead of required.

EventDateTime.description: EventDateTime is one event boundary: an absolute instant plus the IANA time zone it is shown in. DateTime is RFC 3339 with an explicit Z or ±hh:mm offset, such as 2026-02-24T09:00:00-08:00, and TimeZone is an IANA name such as America/Los_Angeles. The offset fixes the instant; TimeZone is the zone the event is written in, so Outlook keeps the organizer's zone. A value without an offset, such as 2026-02-24T09:00:00, or without TimeZone, is rejected rather than guessed. Microsoft Graph itself stores a wall time without an offset plus a zone name. The connector writes the wall time of the instant in TimeZone, or the UTC wall time when a daylight-saving change makes that wall time ambiguous, so the instant never moves. It reads every time back in UTC and returns it with an offset in the requested zone.

dateTime.description: DateTime is the RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is the IANA time zone of the boundary, such as America/Los_Angeles.

inputSchema.description: UpdateEventInput patches named fields of one existing event. A nil field is left unchanged. Start and End are set together and follow the same rules as createEvent.

attendees.description: Attendees replaces the complete attendee list when set; an empty list removes every attendee. Graph sends a meeting update only to the attendees that changed.

body.description: Body replaces the plain-text body when set; an empty string clears it.

end.description: End replaces the exclusive end when set, together with Start.

eventId.description: EventID is the Graph event ID, including an occurrence ID.

isAllDay.description: IsAllDay applies only with Start and End: true makes the event all-day, and false, the default, makes it timed. It is sent whenever Start and End are, so no stale form remains.

location.description: Location replaces the location display name when set; an empty string clears it.

start.description: Start replaces the inclusive start when set, together with End.

subject.description: Subject replaces the title when set; it cannot be blank.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is an optional IANA zone for the offsets of returned times; blank uses Start's zone or UTC.

factories.name: newQueryFreeBusyStep
factories.description: Return the free/busy schedule items and availability view of 1 to 20 users, groups, or rooms in a bounded window through Microsoft Graph getSchedule.

inputSchema.description: QueryFreeBusyInput asks Microsoft Graph getSchedule for the availability of users, distribution lists, or resources in a bounded window.

availabilityViewInterval.description: AvailabilityViewInterval is the length in minutes of each AvailabilityView slot, from 5 to 1440; zero requests 30.

schedules.description: Schedules lists 1 to 20 unique bare SMTP addresses, such as colleague@contoso.com or a room mailbox.

timeMax.description: TimeMax is the required window end as RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. The window must be shorter than 62 days.

timeMin.description: TimeMin is the required window start as RFC 3339 with an explicit offset.

timeZone.description: TimeZone is an optional IANA zone for the offsets of returned intervals; blank uses UTC.
